threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver asks for a contactless payment. Everyone else just flashes their card like it's second nature.
Last week on the 133, a guy in a suit tried to barter with the driver for a free ride after missing his stop. The driver just shook his head, classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing a group of kids argue about which Kebab shop is the best while the scent of currywurst wafts through the street. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, where the walls are covered in local graffiti while you munch on döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to BART delays—if they roll their eyes and keep scrolling on their phone, they’ve been through it all before.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon casually hopping onto the Muni seat, like it owned the place. The passengers barely blinked—classic San Francisco indifference.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the hipster bars, but the real charm is in the quiet afternoons at Plaça de la Vila watching local kids play.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle to choose between 'barça' and 'català' when ordering coffee – they always look a bit lost.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused checking your Oyster card on the bus, while everyone else just swipes and strolls in. Proper Hackney initiation!
Caught a couple arguing about the best jerk chicken in Brixton on the 333 last night. He insisted it’s all in the seasoning. Sounds like a late-night debate!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw the same Turkish grandmother making gözleme every Sunday at the market, always with a smile and that unmistakable love for her craft.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a club that opens at 11 PM for morning yoga. The vibe shifts from zen to rave by midnight—seriously eclectic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their ability to name the best taco shop before the bus even hitches a ride. The rest just ask for directions.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I saw a guy on the 21 bus trying to sell an old iPod while serenading everyone with 'Wonderwall'. Only in the Tenderloin, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think ‘per tanta’ just means ‘for so much’, but it’s a neighborhood code for knowing your bar’s owner if you want a discount.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their enthusiasm for taking photos of every menu item at a tapas bar, totally unaware of the local 'no photos' rule.
